extracted.intended_audience: horror authors, publishers, and members of the Horror Writers Association (HWA); prospective nominees and voters
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing what works are eligible for Bram Stoker Awards, the award categories, how works become nominees, and how winners are chosen and presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — language and publication year
rubrics_metrics.description: Any work of Horror first published in the English language may be considered for an award during the year of its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to works first published in English and considered during the calendar year (or award year) of their publication. The statement is the primary gate for consideration; works not first published in English or not published in the award year are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award philosophy — 'superior achievement' not 'best of the year'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bram Stoker Awards are given 'for superior achievement,' not for 'best of the year,' and the rules are deliberately designed to make ties possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards emphasize recognition of superior accomplishment rather than a single definitive 'best' work; procedures (including tie-allowing rules) are intentionally set to reduce the cutthroat nature of competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories — which forms are eligible and how they are organized
rubrics_metrics.description: The thirteen Bram Stoker Award categories are: Novel, First Novel, Short Fiction, Long Fiction, Young Adult, Middle Grade (added in 2022), Fiction Collection, Poetry Collection, Anthology, Screenplay, Graphic Novel, Nonfiction, and Short Nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories reflect the publishing industry and the horror field; inclusion of categories (e.g., Middle Grade added in 2022) may change over time. Entrants should select or be considered within the appropriate category for their form/length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination pathways — membership recommendations and juries
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two paths to a work becoming a Nominee for the Bram Stoker Award: (1) the HWA membership at large recommends worthy works for consideration, and a preliminary ballot for each category is compiled using a formula based on these recommendations; (2) a Jury for each category also compiles a preliminary ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works can reach the preliminary ballot either via member recommendations (subject to the HWA's formula) or via a category jury. Both routes feed into the preliminary ballot from which subsequent voting proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balloting and voting process — rounds and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Two rounds of voting by our Active members then determine first the Final Ballot (all those appearing on the Final Ballot are 'Bram Stoker Nominees'), and then the Bram Stoker Award Winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After preliminary ballots are compiled (via member recommendations and juries), Active HWA members vote in two rounds: the first round produces the Final Ballot (official nominees), and the second round selects the winners. The page notes a formula is used to compile preliminary ballots but does not publish the formula here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifetime Achievement Awards — criteria for occasional honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifetime Achievement Awards are occasionally presented to individuals whose entire body of work has substantially influenced Horror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These awards are not annual by necessity but are reserved for figures with a demonstrable, substantial influence on the horror genre across their career; consideration is based on body of work rather than a single publication.
